items.stem: A technician measures a home internet connection and records a download of 300 Mbps. What does this unit describe?

options.rationale: Correct: Mbps is megabits per second, a measure of data-transfer rate.
Storage is measured in bytes, not a per-second rate.

options.text: The number of devices allowed on the network
options.rationale: Device count is unrelated to the bits-per-second transfer rate.
Channel numbers identify radio frequencies, not transfer speed.

items.explanation: Correct: Mbps is megabits per second, a measure of data-transfer rate.

items.stem: A user can open a cloud-hosted email service in a browser without installing or patching any server. Which cloud service model is this?

options.rationale: Correct: the provider runs the whole application stack and the user just consumes it.
IaaS gives raw VMs and networks the customer must configure and patch.
On-premises means the customer owns and runs the hardware locally.
PaaS exposes a development platform; the user still deploys their own app code.

items.explanation: Correct: the provider runs the whole application stack and the user just consumes it.

items.stem: Select TWO practices that directly improve the security of a user account.

options.rationale: Correct: a second factor blocks access even if the password leaks.
Correct: length and uniqueness resist guessing and credential-stuffing.

options.text: Sharing the password with a trusted colleague
options.rationale: Sharing credentials removes accountability and widens exposure.

options.text: Reusing one password across all sites
options.rationale: Reuse means one breach compromises every account.

options.text: Disabling the screen lock for convenience
options.rationale: Removing the lock lets anyone with the device use the account.

items.explanation: Correct: a second factor blocks access even if the password leaks. Correct: length and uniqueness resist guessing and credential-stuffing.
